# AgentSwarm.in — full reference

One goal. A governed swarm. Verified work.

## Positioning

AgentSwarm is a control plane for AI workforces. Tell it what needs to get done; it plans the work,
assembles the right specialist agents, executes, blocks on human approval where consequential, and
gives the operator a real, replayable trail of evidence — not a model's self-report of success.

## Architecture

```
React Command Centre
        v HTTP / SSE
Fastify Mission API
        v
PostgreSQL durable state + event store   <-- sole source of truth
        v
Worker (Postgres FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED authoritative claim)
        ^ low-latency wake-up signal only
Redis / BullMQ (coordination, never truth)
        v
Model provider (OpenAI-compatible; shipped with Qwen)
        v
Task outputs -> Artifacts -> Verification -> Mission completion
```

The backend is authoritative. The browser is a projection of persisted state, never the source of
mission truth. If a required model provider is not configured, a mission is honestly marked BLOCKED
with provider status UNAVAILABLE — never simulated as running or completed.

## Mission lifecycle

QUEUED -> PLANNING -> RUNNING -> WAITING_APPROVAL (when required) -> RUNNING -> VERIFYING -> COMPLETED
Terminal/control states also include PAUSED, FAILED, CANCELLED, BLOCKED.
Every transition is server-side validated and produces a persisted event.

## Task lifecycle

QUEUED -> READY -> LEASED -> RUNNING -> SUCCEEDED
Also: WAITING_APPROVAL, RETRY_WAIT, FAILED, CANCELLED, DEAD_LETTER.
Leases are persisted in PostgreSQL; expired leases are recovered by the worker. Retries are bounded
and use exponential backoff before dead-lettering.

## Auth & tenancy

Passwords are hashed with bcrypt. Sessions are opaque random tokens; only a SHA-256 hash of the
token is stored server-side, delivered as an httpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie — never exposed to
client-side JS or stored in localStorage. Every mission belongs to exactly one organization and
project, assigned server-side from a verified membership check the client cannot bypass. Roles are
OWNER > ADMIN > OPERATOR > MEMBER > VIEWER: creating a mission requires MEMBER+, deciding an
approval requires OPERATOR+, creating a project requires ADMIN+. A mission outside the caller's
organizations returns 404, not 403 — existence isn't leaked to non-members.

## Approvals

A task can declare requiresApproval and a risk level (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL). When the worker
reaches such a task, it creates a persisted approval request and the task genuinely stops in
WAITING_APPROVAL. Approving resumes the exact task; rejecting fails the mission. No optimistic
client-side approval — the API is authoritative for the decision.

## Realtime

Every runtime event is inserted into a durable events table with a monotonically increasing
sequence number. A PostgreSQL trigger issues NOTIFY; the API's SSE endpoint listens and streams
matching events to connected clients. Reconnecting clients pass the last event ID and receive
missed events from the durable event store — no duplicate or lost state on reconnect.

## Durable dispatch

Postgres row-level locking (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) is the sole authority on which worker claims a
given mission or task — this holds regardless of how many workers run concurrently. Redis/BullMQ
adds a low-latency wake-up signal on top: after a transaction commits, a lightweight job is
enqueued; the worker's BullMQ consumer reacts by re-running the same claim logic (the job payload
is a hint, never an instruction, so a dropped or duplicate job can't cause duplicate execution). A
slow fallback poll runs independently of Redis and is the only dispatch path when Redis is
unavailable or unconfigured — same correctness, higher latency. This was verified against a real
Redis outage (mission still reached its correct terminal state via the fallback poll alone, and the
API request itself returned in ~1.6s instead of hanging) and a killed-and-restarted worker process
(resumed cleanly with no duplicate events).

## Verification

When every task in a mission succeeds, the mission enters VERIFYING. The current gate checks that
every succeeded task has a persisted artifact before the mission is marked COMPLETED — deliberately
minimal and truthful rather than a decorative green check. Build/typecheck/security verification
gates are on the roadmap as real tool adapters, not yet implemented.

## What is not yet live

MCP tool registry and gateway, sandboxed/isolated task workspaces, persistent memory and reusable
skills, a scheduler for recurring or webhook-triggered missions, a cost engine backed by real
provider-reported usage (current token counts are stored only when the provider returns them —
never fabricated; cost is UNKNOWN rather than guessed), and richer verification gates beyond
artifact-existence.
